content: Choline kinase alpha is an enzyme that is encoded by the CHKA gene in humans. This enzyme plays a critical role in the biosynthesis of phosphatidylcholine, which primarily occurs through the CDP-choline pathway. The protein produced by the CHKA gene functions as the initial enzyme in this biosynthetic sequence and is thought to have a regulatory role in the process. Additionally, this enzyme catalyzes the phosphorylation of ethanolamine, a key step in the synthesis of phospholipids. Two distinct transcript variants of the CHKA gene have been identified, each encoding different isoforms of the enzyme. In melanocytic cells, the expression of the CHKA gene may be regulated by the microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF).
